arashi

Usage: aw|arashi [options] [command]

Git worktree manager for meta-repositories

Options:
  -V, --version                  output the version number
  -h, --help                     display help for command

Commands:
  init [options]                 Initialize Arashi workspace in the current
                                 repository or bootstrap a new one
  install [options]              Install the npm-managed Arashi platform binary
  add [options] <git-url>        Add a Git repository to the workspace; in a
                                 TTY, offers optional repository worktree setup
                                 (default no; --json and --force suppress
                                 setup)
  clone [options]                Clone missing configured repositories
  completion [shell]             Generate native shell completion code
  configure [options]            Inspect or interactively edit supported
                                 workspace configuration
  delete [options] [repository]  Delete configured repository dependencies
  create [options] <branch>      Create coordinated worktrees across multiple
                                 repositories
  doctor [options]               Run non-mutating Arashi workspace diagnostics
  exec [options] [command...]    Run a command once per selected managed
                                 repository
  handoff [options]              Generate a Markdown or JSON handoff report for
                                 the current workspace
  move [options]                 Move uncommitted changes between coordinated
                                 worktrees
  list [options]                 List all worktrees and their status
  status [options]               Show status of all managed repositories
  remove [options] [target]      Remove worktrees and delete branches
  prune [options]                Clean stale Git worktree metadata across the
                                 workspace
  pull [options]                 Pull remote changes across eligible
                                 repositories
  push [options]                 Push coordinated branches across eligible
                                 repositories
  sync [options]                 Align managed repositories to the parent
                                 branch
  uninstall [options]            Conservatively remove a proven Arashi
                                 installation
  shell                          Manage shell integration for parent-shell
                                 switching
  setup [options]                Run setup scripts across workspace
                                 repositories
  switch [options] [filter]      Switch to an existing worktree using explicit,
                                 configured, or contextual modes
  update [options]               Check for and apply Arashi updates
  help [command]                 display help for command
add:
Usage: aw add [options] <git-url>

Add a Git repository to the workspace; in a TTY, offers optional repository
worktree setup (default no; --json and --force suppress setup)

Arguments:
  git-url            Git repository URL (HTTPS, Git, File, [user@]host:path, or
                     ssh://[user@]host/path)

Options:
  -n, --name <name>  Custom repository name
  --create-setup     Create setup.sh template if no setup script found
                     (default: false)
  -f, --force        Skip confirmation prompts (default: false)
  -j, --json         Output result as JSON (default: false)
  -h, --help         display help for command

When stdin and stdout are TTYs, add offers optional repository worktree setup (default: no).
--json and --force suppress setup. Confirmed setup supports copy/symlink paths and inline-or-file lifecycle hooks.
clone:
Usage: aw clone [options]

Clone missing configured repositories

Options:
  --all                            Clone all missing repositories without
                                   interactive selection
  --base <branch>                  Base branch to use when cloning configured
                                   repositories
  --repo-base <repository=branch>  Override the base branch for one selected
                                   repository (repeatable)
  -j, --json                       Output result as JSON; requires --all
  -h, --help                       display help for command
completion:
Usage: aw completion [options] [command] [shell]

Generate native shell completion code

Arguments:
  shell       Shell name (bash, zsh, fish, powershell) (choices: "bash", "zsh",
              "fish", "powershell")

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command
configure:
Usage: aw configure [options]

Inspect or interactively edit supported workspace configuration

Options:
  -j, --json  Inspect supported configured and effective values without
              prompting or mutation
  -h, --help  display help for command

Editing requires TTY stdin and stdout. --json is sanitized inspection only; unsupported fields remain available through direct config.json editing.
create:
Usage: aw create [options] <branch>

Create coordinated worktrees across multiple repositories

Arguments:
  branch                           Branch name to create across repositories

Options:
  --base <branch>                  Base branch to use when creating new target
                                   branches
  --repo-base <repository=branch>  Override the base branch for one selected
                                   repository (repeatable; use @meta for the
                                   meta repository)
  -o, --only <repos>               Only create in specified repositories
                                   (repeatable, comma-separated)
  -g, --group <groups>             Only create in repositories in requested
                                   groups (repeatable, comma-separated)
  -i, --interactive                Interactively select repositories
  --switch                         Switch to the created parent worktree after
                                   create
  --no-switch                      Disable configured create switch defaults
                                   for this invocation
  --launch                         Launch terminal/editor context after create
  --no-launch                      Disable configured create launch defaults
                                   for this invocation
  --tab                            Launch the created worktree in a tab;
                                   bypasses configured launch defaults and
                                   implies --launch and --switch
  --sesh                           Launch using sesh mode (implies --launch)
  --herdr                          Launch using Herdr mode (implies --launch)
  --tmux                           Launch using plain tmux mode (implies
                                   --launch and --switch)
  --conflict <strategy>            Pre-select conflict resolution strategy
                                   (ABORT, REUSE_EXISTING) (choices: "ABORT",
                                   "REUSE_EXISTING")
  --no-hooks                       Disable hook execution
  --no-hook-input                  Execute hooks with input disabled and
                                   immediate EOF
  --no-progress                    Hide progress indicators
  -n, --dry-run                    Show what would be done without making
                                   changes
  --move-changes                   Move compatible uncommitted changes from the
                                   current workspace after create
  -j, --json                       Return structured JSON output for
                                   non-interactive create operations
  -h, --help                       display help for command

Examples:
  $ arashi create feature-branch
  $ arashi create feature-branch --group docs
  $ arashi create feature-branch --only repo1,repo2
  $ arashi create feature-branch --conflict REUSE_EXISTING
  $ arashi create feature-branch --dry-run
  $ arashi create feature-branch --no-launch --no-switch --json

Configured create launch values: none | auto | sesh | herdr
Precedence: --tmux/--sesh/--herdr, --tab/--launch, --no-launch, matching configured scope, then none.
Any enabled launch implies post-create switch handling.
By default, launch opens a new OS window or managed independent-session equivalent.
--tab requests a true tab or equivalent; unsupported mappings fail without opening a window.
delete:
Usage: aw delete [options] [repository]

Delete configured repository dependencies

Arguments:
  repository     Exact configured repository key

Options:
  -f, --force    Confirm deletion and override Git data-loss guards
  -n, --dry-run  Preview the complete deletion plan without mutation
  -j, --json     Output one machine-readable JSON document
  -h, --help     display help for command
doctor:
Usage: aw doctor [options]

Run non-mutating Arashi workspace diagnostics

Options:
  -j, --json  Output a structured JSON envelope
  -h, --help  display help for command

Examples:
  $ arashi doctor          # Human-readable workspace health check
  $ arashi doctor --json   # Automation-safe JSON diagnostics
exec:
Usage: aw exec [options] [command...]

Run a command once per selected managed repository

Arguments:
  command                Command to run after --

Options:
  -o, --only <repo>      Only include a specific repository (repeatable)
  -g, --group <group>    Only include repositories in the requested group
                         (repeatable)
  --dirty                Only include repositories with uncommitted changes
  --jobs <positive-int>  Maximum repositories to run concurrently (default:
                         "1")
  --fail-fast            Stop starting new commands after the first failure
  -j, --json             Output result as JSON
  -h, --help             display help for command
handoff:
Usage: aw handoff [options]

Generate a Markdown or JSON handoff report for the current workspace

Options:
  -j, --json                Output a structured JSON envelope instead of
                            Markdown
  --link <link>             Related issue, PR, spec, or reference link
                            (repeatable)
  --validation <entry>      Validation command and result evidence, e.g. 'pnpm
                            run test — passed' (repeatable)
  --todo <item>             Remaining work item to include as a checklist entry
                            (repeatable)
  --risk <item>             Known risk or blocker to include in the report
                            (repeatable)
  --next-command <command>  Suggested next command, not executed (repeatable)
  -h, --help                display help for command

Examples:
  $ arashi handoff --link https://github.com/corwinm/arashi-arashi/issues/186
  $ arashi handoff --validation "pnpm run test — passed" --todo "watch CI"
  $ arashi handoff --json --next-command "arashi status --verbose"
init:
Usage: aw init [options]

Initialize Arashi workspace in the current repository or bootstrap a new one

Options:
  --repos-dir <path>      Custom location for managed repositories
  --worktrees-dir <path>  Custom worktree base (default: .. for bare
                          repositories; .arashi/worktrees otherwise)
  --ignore-scope <scope>  Managed Git ignore scope: local (default), tracked,
                          or none (choices: "local", "tracked", "none")
  --zero-config           Prepare implicit standalone mode without creating
                          configuration
  -f, --force             Overwrite existing configuration if present
  --no-discover           Skip automatic repository discovery
  -n, --dry-run           Show what would be done without making changes
  -v, --verbose           Show detailed information during initialization
  -j, --json              Output result as JSON
  -h, --help              display help for command

Examples:
  $ arashi init --zero-config           # Standalone .worktrees/ convention only
  $ arashi init                         # Local info/exclude rules (default)
  $ arashi init --ignore-scope tracked  # Team-owned .gitignore block
  $ arashi init --ignore-scope none     # Manual ignore management
  $ arashi init --ignore-scope local    # Reset an existing clone to the default

Existing effective tracked, local, or global rules are honored. Arashi never modifies global Git configuration.
install:
Usage: aw install [options]

Install the npm-managed Arashi platform binary

Options:
  -j, --json  Output result as JSON
  -h, --help  display help for command
list:
Usage: aw list [options]

List all worktrees and their status

Options:
  -v, --verbose        Show detailed sub-repository information
  -j, --json           Output in JSON format
  -t, --table          Show table format with headers (default: simple list)
  --max-depth <depth>  Maximum depth for sub-repo discovery (default: 3)
                       (default: 3)
  -h, --help           display help for command

Examples:
  $ arashi list                    # Simple list of paths (pipe-friendly)
  $ arashi list --table            # Table format with headers
  $ arashi list --json             # Output as JSON
  $ arashi list --verbose          # Show sub-repositories
  $ arashi list | fzf              # Interactive selection with fzf
move:
Usage: aw move [options]

Move uncommitted changes between coordinated worktrees

Options:
  --from <workspace>  Source branch, worktree name, or path
  --to <workspace>    Target branch, worktree name, or path
  -j, --json          Return structured JSON output
  -h, --help          display help for command

Examples:
  $ arashi move --to feature-branch
  $ arashi move --from main --to feature-branch
  $ arashi move --from feature-branch

Usage: aw prune [options]

Clean stale Git worktree metadata across the workspace

Options:
  -n, --dry-run    Report stale worktree metadata without pruning
  --expire <time>  Git worktree prune expiry time (default: "now")
  -j, --json       Output a structured JSON envelope
  -h, --help       display help for command

Examples:
  $ arashi prune --dry-run       # Show stale worktree metadata
  $ arashi prune                 # Prune stale worktree metadata now
  $ arashi prune --json          # Automation-safe prune result

Usage: aw pull [options]

Pull remote changes across eligible repositories

Options:

  -g, --group <group>  Only include repositories in the requested group
                       (repeatable)
  -v, --verbose        Show verbose git output
  -j, --json           Output result as JSON
  -h, --help           display help for command

Usage: aw push [options]

Push coordinated branches across eligible repositories

Options:

  -g, --group <group>  Only include repositories in the requested group

  -h, --help           display help for command

Usage: aw remove [options] [target]

Arguments:

Options:

Usage: aw setup [options]

Run setup scripts across workspace repositories

Options:

  -g, --group <group>  Only include repositories in the requested group
                       (repeatable)

shell:
Usage: aw shell [options] [command]

Manage shell integration for parent-shell switching

Options:
  -h, --help              display help for command

Commands:
  init [options] [shell]  Print shell wrapper code
  uninstall [options]     Remove exact managed shell integration
  install                 Install shell integration into the active shell
                          startup file
  help [command]          display help for command
shell init:
Usage: aw shell init [options] [shell]

Print shell wrapper code

Arguments:
  shell       Shell name (bash, zsh, fish) (choices: "bash", "zsh", "fish")

Options:
  -j, --json  Return a structured unsupported-mode error instead of shell code
  -h, --help  display help for command
shell install:
Usage: aw shell install [options]

Install shell integration into the active shell startup file

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command
shell uninstall:
Usage: aw shell uninstall [options]

Remove exact managed shell integration

Options:
  -n, --dry-run  Inspect the shell removal plan without changing anything
  -y, --yes      Apply the completely preflighted shell removal plan
  -h, --help     display help for command
status:
Usage: aw status [options]

Show status of all managed repositories

Options:
  -v, --verbose        Show full git status output
  -s, --short          Show one-line summary per repository
  -o, --only <repo>    Only include a configured child repository (repeatable,
                       comma-separated)
  -g, --group <group>  Only include repositories in the requested group
                       (repeatable, comma-separated)
  -j, --json           Output a structured JSON envelope
  -h, --help           display help for command

Examples:
  $ arashi status                    # Default output with colors
  $ arashi status --verbose          # Full git status for each repo
  $ arashi status --short            # One line per repository
  $ arashi status --group docs       # Only check repositories in a group
switch:
Usage: aw switch [options] [filter]

Switch to an existing worktree using explicit, configured, or contextual modes

Arguments:
  filter                        Filter targets by branch name or worktree path

Options:
  --path                        Treat argument as exact worktree path
  --sesh                        Use sesh in tmux mode
  --tmux                        Force launch in a new plain tmux window
  --herdr                       Open or focus the selected worktree in Herdr
  --tab                         Opens the selected worktree in a tab and
                                bypasses configured launch defaults
  --cd                          Change the current shell directory when shell
                                integration is active
  --launch                      Launch the selected worktree while preserving a
                                configured launcher
  --vscode                      Open the selected worktree in VS Code
  --cursor                      Open the selected worktree in Cursor
  --kiro                        Open the selected worktree in Kiro
  --ignore-configured-launcher  Bypass a configured sesh or Herdr launcher for
                                this invocation
  --repos                       Use child repositories only
  --all                         Use both parent and child repositories
  -j, --json                    Return a structured unsupported-mode error
                                instead of launching or switching
  -h, --help                    display help for command

Examples:
  $ arashi switch
  $ arashi switch --repos
  $ arashi switch --ignore-configured-launcher
  $ arashi switch --all feature-auth
  $ arashi switch --cursor feature-auth
  $ arashi switch --path /path/to/worktree
  $ arashi switch feature-auth
  $ arashi switch repo-a --sesh

Configured modes: auto | cd | launch | sesh | herdr
Precedence: explicit launcher flags, --cd/--launch, configured mode, then automatic context detection.
By default, launch opens a new OS window or managed independent-session equivalent.
--tab requests a true tab or equivalent; unsupported mappings fail without opening a window.

Usage: aw sync [options]

  -g, --group <groups>  Only sync repositories in requested groups (repeatable,

  -v, --verbose         Show detailed output for each repository
  -j, --json            Output result as JSON
  -h, --help            display help for command
